source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Predict that food moves down the oesophagus because the canal walls contract and relax in waves.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The windpipe contracts and relaxes in waves to push food into the stomach.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Food sliding down the oesophagus makes its walls contract and relax in waves.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Wave-like propulsion occurs only in the oesophagus.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: If a person is upside down, swallowed food cannot reach the stomach.

intelligence.enrichment: The walls of the food pipe contract and relax in a wave-like motion that pushes food down into the stomach; this forward movement occurs throughout the alimentary canal. wave-like contraction and relaxation of canal walls -> food is pushed forward -> food reaches the stomach and later parts of the canal The learner correctly applies this rule: The walls of the food pipe contract and relax in a wave-like motion that pushes food down into the stomach; this forward movement occurs throughout the alimentary canal. Food falls to the stomach by itself once it is swallowed.
